original_identifier: Reader XII. Apollonius of Tyre. The Shipwreck. Two-sentence storm-to-shore extract.
text: Ðǣr-tō-ēacan cōmon ēastnorðerne windas, and se angrīslica sūðwesterna wind him ongēan stōd, and ðæt scip eall tōbærst on ðisse ęgeslican hrēohnesse. Apollonius gefēran ealle forwurdon tō dēaðe, and Apollonius āna becōm mid sunde tō Pentapolim ðǣm Cyreniscan lande, and ðǣr ūpēode on ðǣm strande.

locators.end: 166 editorial line4, first period after on ðǣm strande.
locators.line_convention: On165 count only OE body lines beneath The Shipwreck, starting Apollonius as1; printed marginal5 anchors the immediately preceding line. On166 count from the first prose line; printed marginal5 anchors the following beheold line. Selected line numbers are editorial expansions of Cook’s printed five-line intervals. The source compound crosses165.6–7.

editorial_context.text: Apollonius has embarked for Cyrene. A sudden storm has already disturbed the sea.
editorial_context.purpose: Supplies the antecedent situation for in addition to that without inventing or changing Old English.

independent_audit_translation.literal: In addition to that came northeast winds, and the fierce southwest wind stood against them, and the whole ship broke apart in this terrible tempest. Apollonius’s companions all perished to death, and Apollonius alone came by swimming to Pentapolis, the Cyrenian land, and there came up on the shore.
independent_audit_translation.idiomatic: In addition, northeast winds came, and the fierce southwest wind opposed them; the whole ship broke apart in this terrible storm. All Apollonius’s companions perished, but Apollonius alone swam to Pentapolis, the land of Cyrene, and came ashore there.
independent_audit_translation.method: Prepared independently from the inspected Old English, not copied from a translation or future task key. The idiomatic but renders the contrast expressed by OE and; swam compresses becōm mid sunde.
independent_audit_translation.reference_limit: them is the guiding local reading of him, referring to preceding northeast winds. Context favors it; the spelling alone does not uniquely exclude a singular or other plural referent. A future key should not make that inference an unsupported unique test.

apparatus.text: Lat. (verse): Hinc Notus,hinc Boreas,hinc horridus Africus instat.
apparatus.interpretive_note: The quoted Latin evokes winds from different quarters; it does not explicitly disambiguate the OE pronoun him. Spaces around punctuation are typographical.

apparatus.text: The Latin endings of proper nouns are not always a guide to the case (54). Here we have the genitive.

construction_inventory.description: Two sentences contain six coordinated finite indicative predicates. The final ūpēode retains Apollonius as understood subject; an adverb may precede its verb. No subordinate, imperative, subjunctive, passive, perfect or infinitive construction occurs in the selected span.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Prior coordination and recognition of source order do not impose a universal inversion rule.

construction_inventory.description: tōberstan = break up/go to pieces and forweorðan = perish are intransitive: scip is subject of tōbærst; gefēran is subject of forwurdon. Teach their full checked ClassIII indicative systems as distinct lexemes.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Full finite paradigms are owned by the independent Unit4 grammar audit; no general productive prefix rule or auxiliary use is licensed.

construction_inventory.description: Ðǣr-tō-ēacan means in addition to that/besides: further winds join the already described storm. The preceding storm is summarized in separate English editorial context.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Fixed connective supplied; no productive compound-adverb rule.

construction_inventory.description: him ongēan stōd = stood against/opposed them. ongēan follows its dative pronoun. The natural local reading takes him as the preceding northeast winds, but its spelling also permits masculine/neuter singular and the antecedent is an editorial inference, not morphologically unique.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Do not demand unique number/antecedent identification from him alone; do not teach general postposition syntax. A justified alternative antecedent is not rejected solely for differing from the guiding inference.

construction_inventory.description: ðæt scip eall = the whole ship/all the ship. eall is strong neuter nominative singular, postposed to the subject noun phrase; its morphology/sense were recognition-only in Unit3.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Keep eall morphology and sense at their prior recognition milestone; the postposed whole/all construction is supplied, not independent production.

construction_inventory.description: on ðisse ęgeslican hrēohnesse = in this terrible tempest/storm. The noun phrase is feminine dative singular; ęgeslican is weak after the demonstrative. This abstract surrounding circumstance is supplied locally.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Prior spatial on+dative does not automatically establish every figurative/circumstantial sense.

construction_inventory.description: Apollonius gefēran = Apollonius’s companions. Cook note1 explicitly identifies the foreign proper name here as genitive despite its -us appearance. gefēran is nominative plural, not a subject named Apollonius.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: The relation and before-head placement are prior; the actual foreign-name case form is supplied. No complete Latin-name declension is introduced.

construction_inventory.description: gefēran ealle = all the companions. ealle is strong masculine nominative plural agreeing with gefēran; the all-quantifier construction remains supplied.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Prior recognition of ealle is not new productive quantifier mastery.

construction_inventory.description: forwurdon tō dēaðe = perished to death, naturally all died/perished. dēaðe is masculine dative singular; tō states the endpoint/result, not an infinitive marker or the previously supplied function-for sense.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Supply this tō phrase whole; no general goal/result construction is assumed.

construction_inventory.description: Apollonius āna = Apollonius alone. āna is weak masculine nominative singular of ān in its alone sense, agreeing with the sole survivor; it is not cardinal one or the homographic feminine plural reference form.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: New sense and weak form are supplied only; Unit3 productive cardinal ān does not cover them.

construction_inventory.description: becōm mid sunde = came/arrived by swimming. sund is a neuter noun; sunde is dative singular after mid. This means phrase is not an infinitive or newly productive instrumental construction.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Supply actual mid sunde; do not infer a productive swimming verb or general mid syntax.

construction_inventory.description: tō Pentapolim ðǣm Cyreniscan lande = to Pentapolis, the Cyrenian land. The foreign place name occupies the destination position; the native appositional phrase is neuter dative singular, with weak Cyreniscan. Preserve the foreign -im spelling rather than treating it as a native OE accusative-governance rule.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Exact destination/apposition is supplied. No general foreign-name declension or productive tō-goal syntax.

construction_inventory.description: and ðǣr ūpēode on ðǣm strande = and there he came/went up onto the shore. Apollonius remains the understood subject. ūpēode is the actual anomalous preterite of ūpgān; strande is masculine dative singular in the printed local on phrase.
construction_inventory.scope_limit: Supply ūpēode and ðǣr; preserve dative strande and do not replace it with accusative from a modern English motion gloss.

local_support.text: Ðǣr-tō-ēacan = in addition to that/besides; the storm has already begun.
cōmon = came, third-person plural past of cuman (ClassIV); ēastnorðerne = northeasterly, masculine nominative plural.

angrīslica = fierce/raging; sūðwesterna = southwestern, both weak masculine nominative singular with wind. him ongēan stōd = stood against/opposed them: guiding reference, the northeast winds. The pronoun spelling alone does not exclude a singular referent; no uniquely graded antecedent is required.
eall = whole/all, neuter nominative singular agreeing with scip. This local quantifier use is supplied; its earlier morphology was recognition only.
on ðisse ęgeslican hrēohnesse = in this terrible storm: feminine dative singular; ęgeslican is weak after ðisse.
Apollonius before gefēran is genitive, Apollonius’s, as Cook note1 specifies. ealle = all, masculine nominative plural agreeing with the companions; quantifier use remains supplied.
tō dēaðe = to death, with dative singular dēaðe; the whole expression means that the companions died/perished.

The next Apollonius is nominative. āna = alone, weak masculine nominative singular, a distinct sense/form from cardinal one. becōm = came/arrived (third-person singular past, ClassIV). mid sunde = by swimming: dative noun sunde, not an infinitive.
tō Pentapolim ðǣm Cyreniscan lande = to Pentapolis, the Cyrenian land. Preserve the foreign name; the native apposition is neuter dative singular, with weak Cyreniscan.

ðǣr = there; ūpēode = he came/went up (anomalous past of ūpgān), with Apollonius understood. on ðǣm strande = on the shore, masculine dative singular as printed; do not replace the ending from the English gloss came ashore.

selection_comparison.reason: Opening adds bǣd+infinitive, temporal subordination, ongunnon+infinitive, passives and result clause. The final two sentences provide a coherent storm-to-survival result with simple coordinated indicatives.
Useful occasional strong forms are embedded in questions, directives, subordinate clauses and infinitives; no reason to force those systems into this unit.

reconciliation_conditions: Reconcile the proposed full indicative systems of tōberstan and forweorðan against the independent Unit4 grammar audit before contract release; the source audit establishes their actual forms, senses and intransitive use, not all unattested paradigm cells.
The coordinator must adopt the proposed four full noun systems and exact supplied supports in the saved contract before independent tasks use them. No teaching milestone is created by this audit.

interpretive_limits.resolution: Explicit guiding interpretation supplied; no unique independent test. Both dative singular and plural spellings are already taught, so uncertainty does not hide a missing paradigm.
Supply exact Pentapolim and its destination phrase. Native dative apposition is clear; no regular OE declension is invented.
